newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani rupee ends up in kerb, seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani rupee ends up in kerb, seen rising.

text.p: The Pakistani rupee ended 0.17 up at 41.65 to the dollar in the kerb market on Saturday as traders sold dollars after Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz ruled out any early exchange rate change, dealers said.
The rupee was likely to open higher on Monday, a dealer said.
The State (central) Bank of Pakistan rupee rate, last changed on May 23, was 40.3900/40.5920 against the dollar.
The premium on the foreign exchange bearer certificates closed at 3.40 percent compared to the opening at 3.60 percent.
